case_title: Deny Bora v. State of Assam
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.27
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302, acquitted under TADA
neutral_facts: The accused, a man, was involved in the shooting death of a doctor, who was shot dead in his clinic while attending to patients. The deceased was shot from point blank range, as confirmed by the post mortem report. The prosecution relied on the testimony of a witness, PW-14, who came forward almost two years and eight months after the incident. The witness claimed to be threatened by the co-accused, but the delay in his statement and the lack of corroboration raised doubts about his reliability. The prosecution also failed to examine the deceased's wife and daughter, who were present at the scene and could have provided crucial evidence. The trial court convicted the accused under IPC s.302 based on the testimony of PW-14, but the High Court and Supreme Court found the evidence insufficient and set aside the conviction.
